content.intro: Learn configuring installed applications through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Configuring Installed Applications matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines configuring installed applications as part of django project structure and configuration. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: The INSTALLED_APPS setting; Django's built-in applications; Adding local applications; Registering third-party packages; Application configuration classes. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: The INSTALLED_APPS setting
items.text: `INSTALLED_APPS` activates Django apps and their models, templates, admin registrations, and app configuration. Add the app config or package in accordance with its documentation.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
